company: Bat claimed to be Babe Ruth's 1932 World Series 'called shot' bat
product: Pawn Stars Season 15 clip 'Babe Ruth's 1932 "Called Shot" Bat' (YouTube id GfhnMinDw_o, episode 'Going, Going... Pawn!', aired 2017-10-16). Owner Ricki in Los Angeles asked $2,000,000. Expert Dan Wulkan (Memory Lane Inc.) judged it never used by Babe Ruth, a $200-300 retail bat. No deal.

facts.fact: Owner: this is the bat from the called shot; his father, a serious collector and big Yankee fan, was given the bat.
Owner: Babe Ruth's opening-day Yankee Stadium home run bat sold for about $1.4 million; he puts this bat at $2 million.
Rick: if this is the actual bat, it would be the most expensive Babe Ruth bat.
Owner mentions the called-shot jersey sold for $940,000.
Bat weighs 36.5 oz; Ruth used 36-44 oz bats (good sign). Branded signature identical to expert's 1922 game-used Ruth bat.
Red flags: hand-written name looks like 'CF Dancer' instead of Ruth's; grease pencil date 10/1/32 too clean; 35-inch mark (retail bats only) blackened out.
Expert: absolutely not used by Babe Ruth; a $200-300 bat. Corey: strike one, strike two; 'three strikes, you're out'.
Episode 'Going, Going... Pawn!' aired Oct 16, 2017; crew drove to Los Angeles to see the bat; bat judged fake, worth no more than $300.

The jersey Ruth wore in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series ('called shot') sold for a record $24.12 million at Heritage Auctions in August 2024 (previously sold in 2005 for $940,000 per NPR; CBS says $975,000).
No record found of what happened to this bat after the show.
